entities.name: The Walt Disney Company
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Walt Disney Company is an American multinational mass media and entertainment conglomerate founded in 1923 by Walt Disney and Roy O. Disney in Hollywood, California. The world's largest entertainment company by revenue, it operates film studios, theme parks, streaming services, cable networks, and consumer products divisions touching billions globally.

Walt Disney's innovations transformed animation: 'Steamboat Willie' (1928) introduced synchronized sound to animation, 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs' (1937) proved full-length animated films viable, and Fantasia (1940) demonstrated animation's artistic potential. Disneyland (1955) invented the modern theme park, creating controlled immersive environments for family entertainment that generated entirely new real-estate development patterns.

The company's acquisitions of Pixar (2006), Marvel (2009), Lucasfilm/Star Wars (2012), and 21st Century Fox (2019) created an unprecedented entertainment empire controlling iconic franchises worth hundreds of billions. Disney+ launched in 2019 reached 100 million subscribers faster than any streaming service. Disney's cultural influence spans generations — from Mickey Mouse to The Lion King to Avengers — making it uniquely capable of shaping global popular culture, childhood experiences, and consumer behavior.
